llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate single-file HTML slide generator, but the package metadata doesn't declare runtime binaries (Node/Chrome) while the included scripts execute local binaries and child processes — an incoherence that warrants caution before running.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md and the included scripts (generate, scaffold, markdown-to-content, theme bundles, etc.) are all consistent with a local HTML slide-generation tool that builds single-file, mobile-friendly presentations. The code and documentation align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits behavior to selecting themes, building JSON content, and running local Node scripts to generate HTML and optional preview images. This stays within the described scope. Note: the runtime instructions assume running node scripts and optionally using headless Chrome to render previews; those scripts read filesystem paths you pass (e.g., --content) and spawn child processes (execFileSync). That is expected for this tool but means the agent or user executing it will run local commands and read files referenced by arguments.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only), but the repository includes many Node.js scripts intended to be run directly. The registry metadata declares no required binaries while SKILL.md and the scripts repeatedly call `node` and (for previews) a local Chrome binary. The mismatch (missing declared runtime requirements: Node.js and headless Chrome) is an incoherence that could surprise users and automated installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment credentials or secret variables in metadata. The only environment reference in code is `process.env.CHROME_BIN` (optional override for the Chrome executable path), which is reasonable for a preview-rendering helper. There are no network endpoints or secret-exfiltration indicators in the included files.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request permanent agent-wide privileges. It does not modify other skills' configuration. However, scripts will write generated outputs (HTML, PNG) to the local filesystem when run, which is expected behavior for a generator.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing or running this skill:

- The metadata omitted runtime binaries but the SKILL.md and scripts require Node.js and (optionally) a local Chrome/Chromium for rendering previews. Make sure you have Node installed and, if you plan to use preview rendering, a headless-capable Chrome; otherwise some commands will fail.
- The scripts spawn child processes (execFileSync) and will execute the Node runtime and the configured Chrome binary on your machine. Only run these scripts in environments where you trust the source and where running local binaries is acceptable.
- The generator reads any file paths you pass (e.g., --content path/to.json or --input outline.md). Don’t pass sensitive system file paths to the tool or grant it elevated permissions; it will read and write files under the working directory.
- There are no hidden network calls, credentials, or external download/install steps in the included files — that’s good. Still review the scripts if you plan to run them unattended or let an agent invoke them autonomously.
- Suggested actions: (1) verify Node and Chrome availability and set CHROME_BIN if needed; (2) run scripts in a sandboxed or non-privileged directory first; (3) inspect any script you plan to run for unexpected exec/spawn commands; (4) if you expect the skill to be installable by automated tooling, ask the publisher to declare required binaries (node, chrome) in the metadata to remove the current mismatch.
